newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ hearing told govt building could yet be stopped.
newsitem.headline: NZ hearing told govt building could yet be stopped.

text.p: It was not too late to stop a planned NZ$94 million building to house ministers and support staff, a parliamentary select committee was told on Wednesday.
Asked if the project was past the point of no return, the general manager of Parliamentary Service John O'Sullivan said, "Tenders have not yet been let."
He agreed parliament could still stop the building if the committee reported quickly and that decision was taken by the House.
The select committee is hearing submissions on the new building today and on Thursday after a 200,000 signature petition opposing it was presented to parliament.
The organiser of the petition, Auckland audiologist Susan Grimsdell, was the first to be heard today.
She said the matter should be decided by parliament, not a small group of politicians.
"I would like this petition to force the issue into the House...where it can be debated," she told the committee.
Cabinet in April approved the building, dubbed "the parliamentary palace" by its critics, in the face of strong public opposition to the expenditure and to the demolition of Broadcasting House.
"We can all see the decline in our social services. Should we spend money on an ostentatious building?" Grimsdell asked the committee.

The committee will hear submissions from the Historic Places Trust, the Business Roundtable and property investor Sir Robert Jones, as well as from the minister responsible for the plan, Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon, and groups advocating the
The committee's chairman said it would report to parliament before the end of June.
